CANONICAL_NAME.value: Plain Paxos (Tom Cocagne) -- the essential Paxos roles (Proposer, Acceptor, Learner) and a practical variant with heartbeats and leadership, in Python, with its unit tests

VERSION.value: github.com/cocagne/paxos master as of 2026-09-13 (commit in hashes)

value.lineage: Lamport's Paxos (1989/1998) -- quorum-based, asynchronous, single-decree consensus -- written as small readable classes (essential.py) plus a 'practical' layer (heartbeat-driven leader acquisition, message retransmission, durable state) and a 'functional' variant, each with tests. NOT Raft: no log, no explicit leader term, safety from quorum intersection alone. Widely read as the reference Python Paxos (the Java twin lives in src/).

value.built_to: let a majority of unreliable nodes agree on one value despite crashes and message loss, and keep agreeing when a leader dies
value.pressure: asynchrony, crash failures, duelling proposers (livelock is Paxos's known liveness hazard, which the practical layer's leader heartbeats exist to suppress)
value.success_means: no two learners learn different values; a value is learned once a quorum is available

value.pressure: partial failure, message loss, competing proposers
value.failure_condition: duelling proposers never decide (liveness), or -- if the quorum rule is broken -- two values decided (safety)

ANCESTRY.value: Lamport's Paxos (1989/1998) -- quorum-based, asynchronous, single-decree consensus -- written as small readable classes (essential.py) plus a 'practical' layer (heartbeat-driven leader acquisition, message retransmission, durable state) and a 'functional' variant, each with tests. ancestry_edges.note: Raft (2014) is a redesign of Paxos for understandability; this is the ancestor family
